cards.text: Jesus, God's Son, just finished telling a story about a nobleman who goes away to become king (Luke 19:11-27). Now He goes on ahead, going up to Jerusalem. Near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sends out two of His disciples.

cards.question: Jesus sends two disciples into the village ahead. What does He say they'll find tied up there?
Jesus tells the two disciples that no one has ever sat on this colt.

cards.text: Jesus tells them to untie it and bring it to Him. He even gets them ready for the awkward moment when somebody asks, “Why are you untying it?”

cards.question: If anyone asks the two disciples why they're untying the colt, what does Jesus tell them to say?

answers.text: We will bring it back soon

cards.text: So the two head out, and they find it just as Jesus had told them. Friend, when MY phone says “You have arrived,” I'm staring at an empty parking lot.

cards.question: As the disciples are untying the colt, its ___ ask them why they're untying it.
When the owners ask why, the two disciples answer with the line Jesus gave them: The Lord needs it.

cards.text: They lead the colt to Jesus, throw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it. No saddle? No problem, friend, those cloaks just got PROMOTED.

cards.question: As Jesus rides along on the colt, what do the people spread on the road?

cards.text: As Jesus approaches the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples starts praising God joyfully in a loud voice. And I mean LOUD, friend, like a stadium when the home team scores.

cards.question: The whole crowd of disciples is praising God joyfully as Jesus approaches the descent from the Mount of Olives. What are they praising Him for?

answers.text: All the miracles they had seen

cards.question: As they praise God, what do the disciples call the One who comes in the name of the Lord?

cards.text: They shout, “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!” But some of the Pharisees, a group of strict religious teachers, are in the crowd, and they've got a request for Jesus.

cards.question: Some Pharisees in the crowd call Jesus Teacher and ask Him to ___ His disciples.

cards.text: The Pharisees want the volume turned DOWN. Jesus doesn't touch the knob. He answers them right there in the middle of all that noise, and I bet they did NOT see this one coming.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if His disciples remain silent, something else will cry out. What is it?

cards.text: All that praise on the road, and now Jesus comes near Jerusalem. He sees the city.

cards.question: As Jesus approaches Jerusalem and sees the city, what does He do?

answers.text: He sings a psalm over it
He blesses it with a shout

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace!” The crowd is shouting about peace in heaven, and Jesus is talking about the peace this city missed.

cards.question: Jesus says that what would bring Jerusalem peace is now hidden from its eyes.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks ahead. He says the days will come when the city's enemies will barricade it, surround it and hem it in on every side.

cards.question: Jesus says the city's enemies will surround Jerusalem but leave its walls standing.
Why does Jesus say all this will come on Jerusalem?

answers.text: It did not recognize God's visit
It did not keep the Sabbath
It made peace with its enemies

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 8 choice cards: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin, including three runs of back-to-back multiple choice (cards 2-3, 7 and 9, and 14).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question asks which title fills the shouted line 'Blessed is the ___ who comes in the name of the Lord' (King, Prophet or Priest). This tests the wording of a quoted line, not meaning. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward King over Prophet or Priest, so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Story card 9 has just told that the disciples threw their cloaks over the colt, and its joke is about those cloaks. That makes 'Their cloaks' the obvious pick for what the people spread on the road, so the right answer stands out against 'Sackcloth' and 'Fine linen'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'when MY phone says “You have arrived,” I'm staring at an empty parking lot' gives Papa Dorin a phone and has him driving to parking lots. In the backstory, he lives alone on a cookie planet just big enough for his bakery. papa-dorin.md lets him use phones and traffic for comparisons and lets jokes make up small habits around his bakery. It also says he never adds anything new to his world. It doesn't say whether a joke can claim a first-person everyday-life experience outside the bakery.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes describe himself personally using everyday adult things like a phone, GPS or driving, or should those stay as general comparisons (for example, 'when your phone says...')?
